title: bls12-381-fixed-g2-invert-g1: mixed squaring/multiplication Frobenius-class parallel Pollard rho in GT, success target 0.39

claims.statement: For uniform nonidentity Q in G2 and uniform z in GT, the algorithm in proof.md (public submission 3da91365-2d58-40e5-ac7d-415e3061f7d8's design: compute g=e(P0,Q); solve z=g^x by parallel distinguished-point Pollard rho on the 12-element Frobenius classes of GT with R=1024 twisted multipliers, a 4-Fp-multiplication canonical-conjugate key, partition and distinguished bits taken from the raw class key, deterministic class-consistent fruitless-cycle escape and a 40/theta stuck-walk restart; output P=[x]P0 and verify e(P,Q)=z) succeeds with probability at least 0.39 using at most 2^125.767 total dense-Fp12-multiplication equivalents (C=20,000), including setup, pairings, table construction, walk starts, distinguished-point handling, cycle handling, detection delay, output and verification. The walk is mixed: a step is a cyclotomic squaring when bits 198..207 of the class key K, read as a 10-bit value, are below 1024*f with f=1/2, and otherwise a dense multiplication by a twisted table entry. GT lies in the cyclotomic subgroup (r divides p^4-p^2+1), Granger-Scott squaring of a walk element is 9 Fp2 squarings plus 12 Montgomery reductions, about 0.80 units including the key block that every step computes, against 1.14 units for a multiplication step; the mean step is 0.97058 units (the squaring price uses redc_mont_384 = 200; proof.md section 6 gives the 125.740-125.798 bracket at 120..300 and states that the bound holds for redc_mont_384 <= about 202); the toy measurement of the mixed map against a multiplication-only control in the same harness (three fields near 2^20, R = 64, 256, 1024, 200 instances per cell, pooled fraction within 1.03 S0 of the 0.39 budget 0.372 against 0.418) implies the mixed walk needs about 8% more steps for the same success, so the ledger charges the 10% step inflation as extra steps: the walk-step cap is 1.10 x 1.000435 x S = 1.1335 S0 = 2^125.8093 steps, at which the measured 1.080 ratio puts the effective budget at 1.050 S0 and the random-mapping model gives success 0.4199. The step type is a function of the class alone, so two walks that reach the same class take identical steps and stay merged, which is what keeps the parallel distinguished-point collision search at its square-root work. Peak memory is below 2^73 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^31 units and is included; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. The success bound relies on the standard random-mapping heuristic for R-adding rho walks (with the Brent-Pollard R/(R-1) correction and 3% explicit step slack; model success 0.4081 at S = 1.03 S0 and 0.4199 at the capped budget) and on the same heuristic for the mixed map, which is measured against a multiplication-only control in the same toy harness on three fields near 2^20 at R = 64, 256 and 1024; no production-size run is claimed. The fruitless-cycle rates are derived, not asserted, and a squaring cannot close a short cycle.

experiments.purpose: Part A: on real BLS12-381 GT elements, check r divides p^4-p^2+1 (GT is in the cyclotomic subgroup), the Frobenius formula, the 4-multiplication conjugate-key formula, distinctness of the 12 keys, consistency of the canonical representative, p^6 = inversion, ord_r(p)=12, and that squaring commutes with Frobenius, never lands on its own class and is an injection on classes because r is odd. Part B: run the complete walk (kappa trick, twisted table, partition h = K mod R and distinguished test on the raw class key as in production, class-determined squaring steps at fraction mix_1024/1024, 2-cycle and checkpoint escapes, stuck-walk rule, collision solving) in a field q near 2^20 with the same tower shape, and report collision times against the 0.39 budget S0 and 1.03 S0, the realised squaring fraction, cycle rates and the distinguished fraction; mix_1024 = 0 is the multiplication-only control. Part C: recompute the fruitless-cycle bound and the per-step ledger for both step kinds, and check the submitted claim against log2 W for the charged squaring fraction. Toy scale only; does not validate production costs.
